analysis.title: Asset Allocation Insights, Issue 114: Earnings deliver, AI spends, central banks wait, markets rotate
key_insights: October was a central bank pause month. The Fed (28 Oct), ECB (29 Oct) and BoJ (30 Oct) all held after September hikes, but none closed the door to further hikes.
The Fed held at 3.75%-4.00% on 28 October. Governor Cook and Cleveland Fed President Hammack dissented in favour of an immediate hike. Cook had been regarded as a dove and had never dissented before.

Chair Warsh said the September hike is starting to restrain activity, rejected forward guidance again, and said some FOMC meetings from 2027 will be devoted to strategy rather than rate decisions. The tone kept a December hike priced in.
First-half US GDP growth was revised up from 1.8% to 2.4%. The advance Q3 estimate was 3.4% annualised.

The US 10-year yield reached about 5.3% in early October, the highest since 2002, then fell to about 5.0% by 29 October as investors bought Treasuries during the AI-stock sell-off. The 10-year TIPS yield fell to about 2.6% from almost 3.0%.
September US CPI (published 14 October) showed headline inflation at 3.7% y/y and core at 2.6%, with diesel and other motor fuel up more than 60% y/y.

The French 10-year yield rose above 5% for the first time since 2002 and the spread over Bunds widened to about 155 basis points ahead of the April 2027 presidential election. Syz avoids French government debt.

The ECB held its deposit rate at 2.50% on 29 October, citing tighter financing conditions and energy-driven upside inflation risk, with Eurozone inflation at 3.8% in September. Lagarde will step down on 7 February 2027.
The BoJ held at 1.25% in an 8-1 vote, with one member calling for a hike to 1.5%. It raised its inflation forecast and signalled further tightening.

The S&P 500 closed above 7,800 for the first time in early October and pulled back to about 7,720 by 29 October. Q3 S&P 500 earnings are up about 29.5% y/y, 83% of companies beat estimates, ten of eleven sectors are growing, and forward EPS is a record near USD 411.
The pullback is described as a rotation. On 29 October Alphabet fell more than 12% while the Russell 2000 hit a three-week high and eight of eleven S&P 500 sectors closed higher.

Hyperscaler Q3 results: Azure grew 48%, Google Cloud more than doubled to USD 30.7bn with a backlog of about USD 561bn, AWS grew 39%, and Meta ad revenue rose 26%. Combined quarterly capex of Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft and Meta was about USD 202bn in Q3, up from about USD 165bn in Q2 and roughly double a year ago.

The market separated hyperscalers that fund capex from operating cash flow from those that cannot. Microsoft (capex about USD 45bn, below guidance) rose. Meta fell 7% on 22 October after capex of USD 34.9bn exceeded operating cash flow, free cash flow turned negative, and it launched about USD 37.5bn of stock issuance. Its five-year CDS touched a record.

Alphabet fell more than 12% on 29 October as search growth slowed to 12%, capex reached USD 51.4bn, and free cash flow was negative for a second quarter. Amazon fell about 7% after hours on Q3 capex of USD 77.3bn, with 2027 spending to be meaningfully above the roughly USD 220bn planned for 2026.

Syz views the AI cycle as entering a more capital-intensive and selective phase, where credit markets rather than earnings alone decide how far the build-out goes. The four hyperscalers spent about USD 500bn on capex in the first nine months of 2026.

Brent ranged between about USD 100 (7 Oct) and USD 117 (23 Oct, highest close since April). Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure, unconfirmed reports of mines in the Strait of Hormuz and a drop in tanker flows pushed prices up after a G7 release of up to 100 million barrels. Talks in Tehran on 26 October opened a diplomatic channel with no agreement yet.
Gold dipped below USD 4,000 on 23 October and recovered to about USD 4,030, helped by lower Treasury yields.
The US midterms (3 November) coincide with an OPEC+ meeting on 1 November. Press reports say Washington asked Gulf states to prepare for a possible short campaign against Iran after the vote.

Syz expects a Fed hike in December and one more in H1 2027, while markets price one and a half hikes in 2027. It expects the Fed, ECB, BoJ and BoE to hike twice by next summer and the SNB once. October payrolls and CPI will confirm or challenge the December call.
Scenario probabilities: Indian summer baseline cut from 45% to 40%, growth freeze raised from 15% to 20%, inflation heatwave unchanged at 40%.

Pillars: Macro Cycle lowered from moderately positive to neutral, Market Factors raised from moderately positive to positive, Liquidity neutral, Earnings growth positive, Valuations neutral. No change to the asset allocation grid.

Positioning: neutral equities, overweight cash, underweight fixed income (moderate underweight in 1-10 year governments, underweight 10 years and above), neutral corporate IG, high yield and EM debt, all major currencies underweight against the USD, overweight gold and commodities, neutral hedge funds.
Valuation: S&P 500 forward P/E is 18.5x versus 23x a year ago (18.1x on 2027 estimates). Europe is at 14.7x, Japan 16.4x and emerging markets 10.4x. The US earnings-yield cushion over bonds is thin.

Four signals would turn Syz defensive: financial conditions biting, negative earnings revisions, weakening technicals, and AI capex funding breaking down. Three are green. The credit signal is amber, with CCC spreads near 11.3% and high-yield CDS above their rising 200-day averages for a third week, with no spillover yet into investment grade or BBB.

Syz would buy weakness once high-yield spreads turn, and would reconsider its neutral equity stance if stress moves up the quality ladder. It favours companies that fund investment from operating cash flow.

earnings_insights: Q3 S&P 500 earnings growth is about 29.5% y/y with most of the index reported. 83% of companies beat estimates and ten of eleven sectors are growing. Surprises are smaller and guidance increasingly drives stocks.
Forward S&P 500 EPS is a record of about USD 411, and forward operating margins are at all-time highs in every region.
2026 consensus EPS growth expectations are 34.4% for the US, 22.8% for Europe and 25.5% for Japan. 2027 growth forecasts are 15.8%, 8.7% and 14.6% respectively.
Meta Q3: capex USD 34.9bn exceeded operating cash flow, free cash flow turned negative, 2026 capex guidance floor raised to USD 135bn, advertising revenue +26%.
Alphabet Q3: Google Cloud revenue more than doubled to USD 30.7bn with a backlog of about USD 561bn, search growth slowed to 12%, capex USD 51.4bn, free cash flow negative for a second quarter.
Amazon Q3: AWS grew 39%, capex USD 77.3bn well above expectations, 2027 spending to be meaningfully higher than the roughly USD 220bn planned for 2026.
Microsoft Q3: Azure grew 48%, capex about USD 45bn below guidance.
Nvidia's results in November are the next checkpoint for AI capex funding.

vol_and_positioning: High-yield CDS have stayed above their rising 200-day averages for a third week, and CCC spreads widened to about 11.3%, with no spillover into investment grade or BBB credit.
The US market factor raw score rebounded to 82%, with nine of eleven indicators positive. Only rate of change and the put/call ratio remain negative.
The European market factor raw score held at 60%, with six of ten indicators positive. Rate of change, MACD, put/call ratio and volume are negative.
Market breadth remains constructive without the large negative divergences that typically precede major tops.
geopolitical: Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and airports, unconfirmed reports of mines in the Strait of Hormuz and a sharp drop in tanker flows pushed Brent to about USD 117.
A G7 agreement to release up to 100 million barrels of crude and diesel initially eased oil prices.
Meetings in Tehran on 26 October between Iran's president and Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish officials opened a new diplomatic channel with no agreement in sight.
Press reports say Washington asked Gulf states to prepare for a possible short campaign against Iran after the 3 November US midterms.
An OPEC+ meeting on 1 November coincides with the midterms.
French political uncertainty is rising ahead of the April 2027 presidential election.
US tariffs and retaliatory measures continue to weigh on global trade momentum, below the H1 2026 peaks.

tension_points.bull_case: Cloud demand is accelerating (Azure +48%, AWS +39%, Google Cloud backlog about USD 561bn), and Microsoft rose after reporting capex below guidance. Syz sees hyperscaler funding as sound overall.
tension_points.bear_case: Combined capex of about USD 202bn in Q3 is rising faster than cash flow. Meta and Alphabet had negative free cash flow, Meta issued equity and its CDS hit a record, and some smaller AI infrastructure providers saw credit spreads widen.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Credit stress spreading from CCC issuers into investment grade, or a breakdown in the funding of AI capex, would push Syz to reconsider its neutral equity stance.

tension_points.bull_case: Q3 GDP growth of 3.4% annualised, upgraded activity language and Warsh's rejection of forward guidance keep a December hike priced in.
tension_points.bear_case: The September hike is starting to restrain activity, with credit tightening for some businesses and households, and early signs that energy prices are cutting into consumption.
tension_points.what_invalidates: October payrolls and October CPI will confirm or challenge the December hike view.

theme_stances.key_argument: The shift from self-funded to externally funded capex makes credit markets, rather than earnings alone, the arbiter of how far the AI build-out can go.

theme_stances.key_argument: Syz expects a Fed hike in December and one more in the first half of 2027, which is a measured adjustment rather than an aggressive cycle.
theme_stances.evidence: Central banks have paused, not pivoted.

theme_stances.key_argument: The pullback is a rotation within equities rather than a broad retreat from risk, and earnings rather than multiples are carrying the market.
